newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritian minister to stay, quits opposition group.
newsitem.headline: Mauritian minister to stay, quits opposition group.

text.p: Mauritius Minister of Land, Transport, Shipping and Public Safety Rashid Beebeejaun said on Monday he had resigned from the opposition Mouvement Militant Mauricien and would stay on as minister.
The MMM resigned from the Indian Ocean island's governing coalition over the weekend and its leader Paul Berenger said the party would assume an opposition status.
"I have signified to the prime minister my intention to stay with the government in order to provide any help I can in the major task that lies ahead," Beebeejaun told reporters.
On Sunday, Mauritius President Cassim Uteem accepted the resignation of eight ministers and four junior ministers, all members of the MMM, from the government of the Indian Ocean island republic.

Conflict has been growing over the past 15 months between the Labour party, led by Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam and which won 35 seats in the December 1995 elections, and the MMM which won 25 seats.
Last June the MMM attacked the 1996/97 budget of Finance Minister Rundheersing Bheenick, and later forced his resignation.
The two parties have been openly critical of each other.
On Labour Day (May 1), each party had its own public meeting, with Berenger declaring that the MMM would would act as watchdog within the government -- invoking the fury of Ramgoolam.
After subsequent criticism of the l997/98 budget, Ramgoolam invited the MMM to assume the role of the opposition.

Last week, on Ramgoolam's recommendation, president Uteem revoked Berenger's appointment as deputy prime minister. In a gesture of solidarity, 12 of the 13 MMM ministers announced they had resigned to lead the opposition.

The Labour Party and MMM took all 60 seats in the national assembly in the December 1995 general elections, defeating former Prime Minister Aneerood Jugnauth's MSM alliance which had ruled for 13 years.
